answer: It is necessary to evaluate both group and individual fairness in recommender systems because metrics for one granularity level cannot be used as a proxy for the other; specifically, group fairness metrics cannot estimate individual fairness. This means that if only one type of fairness is evaluated, it may lead to an incomplete understanding of the system's fairness, potentially overlooking disadvantages faced by specific individuals or groups. Evaluating both types ensures that no groups or individuals are systematically discriminated against.
